name: Primary cutaneous follicle centre lymphoma
theme: the skin-limited entity · the over-treatment lesson

meta.title: PCFCL in silico decision trainer
meta.condition: Primary cutaneous follicle centre lymphoma, adult
meta.population: Adults with PCFCL - the SKIN-LIMITED follicle-centre entity (~11% of all cutaneous lymphomas, the commonest cutaneous B-cell lymphoma - consensus-sourced), guarded by TWO KILLER CONFUSABLES: primary cutaneous DLBCL leg-type (an AGGRESSIVE different disease - 5-yr disease-specific survival 41%, verified - whose delay kills) and SYSTEMIC follicular lymphoma with secondary skin involvement (the follicular trainer's patient - a LIVE reroute, the registry's sixth). The disease itself is among oncology's gentlest: 5-yr disease-specific survival ~95%, skin relapses in ~30% WITHOUT survival cost - and THE OVER-TREATMENT LESSON is verified at its source: multiagent chemotherapy equaled radiotherapy on every outcome with ZERO lymphoma deaths (Bekkenk, verified) - chemotherapy adds toxicity, not survival, in skin-limited disease.
meta.summary: Evidence-linked teaching application for the registry's gentlest lymphoma and emptiest trial census. THE TWO KILLER CONFUSABLES are the architecture: leg-type (verified: 5-yr DSS 41%, BCL2-strong, elderly-leg-predominant, treated R-CHOP-style - a different disease honestly BLOCKED because its trainer does not exist) and systemic follicular with skin involvement (the LIVE reroute to the follicular trainer - staging exists to find exactly this patient). THE METHOD-DEPENDENT BIOMARKER is taught with both receipts: t(14;18) is classically ABSENT in PCFCL (verified: 0/36 by PCR-era methods) - and…
meta.disclaimer: Synthetic teaching environment. Not medical advice; every number is a claim with a citation and an expiry date.
meta.classification: WHO-EORTC cutaneous lymphoma classification (2005 original + 2018 update - both PMID-verified, with three near-title traps caught); WHO5 + ICC 2022 retain PCFCL (verified); ISCL/EORTC TNM for non-MF cutaneous lymphoma (verified) - T1-T2 (solitary/regional) vs T3 (multifocal) as the extent axis
meta.response: Clinical skin assessment; the relapse vocabulary matters: SKIN relapse (~30%, survival unaffected) and EXTRACUTANEOUS dissemination (~10%, secondhand-flagged - the event that changes trainers) are different events with different meanings, and the trainer keeps them separate

Newly diagnosed.name: Definitive local radiotherapy (T1-T2 - the standard receipt)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: the T1-T2 standard (EORTC/ISCL consensus verified; NCCN secondhand)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: large retrospective series (verified receipts) - the disease's gentleness has never needed an RCT, and the census confirms none exists
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: local skin effects in a tight field - cosmesis-aware planning is part of the prescription
Newly diagnosed.patient: For one spot or one region: a short course of focused radiation - the standard treatment, with survival essentially unaffected by this disease afterward.

Newly diagnosed.name: Excision with observation (the biopsy may suffice)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: a consensus option for solitary excised lesions (verified consensus; series receipts flagged)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: consensus grade (the dedicated series did not match - said)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: a scar - which in this disease is a real consideration, not a footnote
Newly diagnosed.patient: If the biopsy removed the whole spot: careful watching may be the entire treatment.

Newly diagnosed.name: Low-dose RT, 2x2 Gy (the cosmesis option - and the dose correction)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: an option for multifocal/cosmesis-critical/re-treatment settings (series grade)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: small prospective-adjacent series (verified) - CRR-labeled: displays, never ranks
Newly diagnosed.patient: A two-visit micro-dose of radiation: clears most treated spots with essentially no side effects, and can be repeated - the gentlest tool in the box.

Newly diagnosed.name: The multifocal strategy (rituximab-based - and the over-treatment lesson)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: the T3 standard (consensus verified) - chemotherapy explicitly NOT part of it
Newly diagnosed.evidence: series grade both routes (verified) + the verified over-treatment receipt
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: minimal - infusion/injection logistics; the lesson is what is NOT on this card
Newly diagnosed.patient: For many spots: the antibody - injected into lesions or given by vein - often with micro-dose radiation to chosen spots; chemotherapy is deliberately absent, because the studies show it adds side effects without adding survival.

Newly diagnosed.name: Comfort-focused care / deferred treatment
Newly diagnosed.guideline: always on the menu - and in this disease, sometimes simply reasonable
Newly diagnosed.patient: Choosing not to treat is genuinely reasonable in some situations here - this disease rarely threatens life either way.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: The gentle loop (skin relapse - same toolbox, same results)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: the skin-relapse convention (consensus verified) - the loop, not an escalation
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: the frontline receipts re-apply (verified); the flagged median says teaching estimate
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: same as frontline - gentle by construction
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: A return on the skin re-opens the same gentle menu - and the outlook stays excellent.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Extracutaneous spread (the trainer-change fork)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: the dissemination convention: re-verify, then the systemic row's rules
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: teaching estimate (flagged); the neighbor trainer's receipts govern from here
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: If the disease ever appears beyond the skin: a fresh biopsy and full re-mapping first - then the plan follows the body-wide follicular lymphoma playbook, which has its own trainer and its own gentle-when-possible logic.

refs.label: WHO-EORTC cutaneous lymphoma classification: 2005 original (Willemze, Blood 2005;105:3768-85 - PMID 15692063, pubmed-url-match; the Burg near-title 16293178 caught) + 2018 update (Willemze, Blood 2019;133:1703-14 - PMID 30635287, pubmed-url-match; a citation-styled duplicate at 31558559 caught). WHO5 (35732829) + ICC (35653592) retain PCFCL - the trap-pair entries caught AGAIN (fourth consecutive run) | PMID 30635287 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-26

NCCN Primary Cutaneous Lymphomas guideline (CBCL pathway: skin-directed for T1-T2, rituximab for extensive) - SECONDHAND, dated (~2025 versions, not fetched); NCI PDQ has NO PCFCL-specific summary (stated as likely-nonexistent, unverified)

The indolent truth: 5-yr disease-specific survival ~95% (consensus language; Senff 300-patient CBCL reclassification - PMID 17353548, pubmed-url-match - the good-prognosis receipt with leg-localization/FOXP1 as the adverse flags); skin relapse ~30% without survival cost (verified framing); extracutaneous dissemination ~10% (SECONDHAND-FLAGGED - primary-series attribution unmatched) | PMID 17353548 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-26

Definitive RT receipt: Senff 153-patient WHO-EORTC-classified radiotherapy series (PMID 18087001, TITLE-matched; journal/year at memory grade - FLAGGED); de-escalated-RT series (31758232, title-matched) | PMID 18087001 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-26

THE DOSE CORRECTION, logged: the low-dose cutaneous-B receipt is 2x2 GY (4 Gy total) - Neelis (PMID 18834672, pubmed-url-match): 18 CBCL patients (10 PCMZL/8 PCFCL), 44 lesions, CR 72%; the 8-Gy schedule in that study was the CTCL escalation - the authoring premise ('2x4 Gy') arrived wrong and the sweep corrected it (the second premise catch in three runs). Fresh support: 2025 multicenter low-dose series + 2026 ILROG dataset (both secondhand) | PMID 18834672 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-26

Rituximab receipts at series grade: intralesional Spanish multicentre (PMID 22356294, Br J Dermatol 2012;167(1), abstract re-read firsthand 2026-09-10): 35 patients, 18 follicle-centre and 17 marginal-zone; complete response 71% and partial response 23% ACROSS BOTH histologies, with the paper stating only that 'similar response rates were observed' in the two - it publishes no follicle-centre-specific figure; median time to complete response 8 weeks at 10 mg per lesion, median disease-free survival 114.1 weeks, most frequent adverse event localised injection-site pain. The previously displayed 'FCL response 100%, CR 80%' appears nowhere in the publication; systemic rituximab in indolent PCBCL (18817999, title-matched); intralesional-vs-IV (36230709) + first intralesional series (10724200) matched. The intralesional-steroid series did NOT match - consensus-grade, FLAGGED | PMID 22356294 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-26

THE OVER-TREATMENT LESSON at its verified source: Bekkenk, treatment of multifocal PCBCL, 29 patients (JCO 1999 - PMID 10561311, pubmed-url-match): multiagent CHEMOTHERAPY equaled radiotherapy on CR, relapse, AND survival; 1/24 extracutaneous progression; ZERO lymphoma deaths at median 54 months - chemotherapy adds toxicity, not survival, in skin-limited disease. Codified in the EORTC/ISCL consensus (18567836, matched) | PMID 10561311 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-26

EORTC/ISCL consensus recommendations for CBCL management (Senff, Blood 2008 - PMID 18567836, pubmed-url-match): skin-directed first-line for skin-limited PCFCL; systemic chemo reserved; staging at diagnosis (the confusable-hunt) - explicitly a retrospective/small-cohort evidence base, said. The 2025 EORTC/USCLC/ISCL update (BJD - secondhand) is the fresh anchor | PMID 18567836 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-26

ISCL/EORTC TNM for non-MF cutaneous lymphoma (Kim, Blood 2007 - PMID 17339420, pubmed-url-match): T1 solitary / T2 regional / T3 multifocal - the extent axis. The PET/CT-specific primary receipt is WEAK (FLAGGED - consensus practice, secondhand) | PMID 17339420 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-26

THE SPLIT STAGING LITERATURE, both sides: consensus stages everyone (18567836) - AND 'Staging of PCFCL: bone marrow biopsy, CD10, BCL2 and t(14;18) are not relevant prognostic factors' (PMID 30998188, pubmed-url-match) doubts the yield; the Senff marrow-relevance counter-paper did NOT match (FLAGGED). Genuinely divided - carried as divided, consensus practice holding meanwhile | PMID 30998188 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-26

THE METHOD-DEPENDENT BIOMARKER, both receipts: t(14;18) absent 0/36 PCBCL vs 3/4 systemic-FL-in-skin (PMID 11298531, pubmed-url-match - the classic separation receipt) AND FISH finds IGH-BCL2 in ~41% of true PCFCL (PMID 16625101, pubmed-url-match - the counterpoint). Plus the primary-vs-secondary comparative receipt (30511443, matched). Teaching: strong BCL2/t(14;18) RAISES suspicion and hardens staging - calibration, not absolutism | PMID 16625101 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-26

PCDLBCL LEG-TYPE - the killer confusable's receipts: Grange 60-case series (Arch Dermatol 2007 - PMID 17875875, pubmed-url-match): 5-yr DSS 41%, leg site 72%, BCL2 85%, mean age 76, frequent extracutaneous spread; rituximab-era improvement with R-CHOP-based therapy (JAMA Dermatol 2014 - PMID 24647650, matched). A DIFFERENT DISEASE whose delay kills - blocked honestly (no trainer exists); leg-type PET receipt (32209875) matched | PMID 17875875 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-26

THE EMPTIEST CENSUS (web-verified 2026-08-19, all statuses re-check due): ZERO interventional trials name PCFCL anywhere; the only entity-naming entry (NCT07310745) is a retrospective, NON-enrolling Italian chart review (active-not-recruiting; readout 2026 will be the largest registered low-dose dataset); checked-and-not-fits: the Fred Hutch mosunetuzumab pilot (FL/MZL only) and MDACC MZL studies. The absence reflects the disease's gentleness - stated as the lesson, not a gap

USCLC National Cutaneous Lymphoma Registry + Clinical Trials Network (usclc.org - the real US infrastructure for this disease; the Connect registry NCT04982471's cutaneous-B inclusion unverified) - WEB-VERIFIED 2026-08-19, re-check due; the 2025 EORTC/USCLC/ISCL consensus (BJD) + 2026 ILROG RT dataset (Blood 147:3051) are the fresh evidence anchors (secondhand)

MSK 25-089 (NCT07029217): phase 3 randomized, standard 24 Gy vs PET-guided very-low-dose 4 Gy staged RT, untreated stage 1-2 indolent B-NHL - RECRUITING (est. completion 2028) - CUTANEOUS DOOR UNCONFIRMED: public page lists FL/MZL; ILROG-cutaneous language suggestive only; PER-PROTOCOL INQUIRY REQUIRED (the MSK VLDRT 4 Gy series + ASH 2024 abstract are the antecedents) - WEB-VERIFIED 2026-08-19

Mayo POSEIDON (NCT06386315): phase 2 randomized, reduced-dose hypofractionated RT (8-10 Gy in 2-5 fx) vs 24 Gy/12, indolent B-NHL - RECRUITING (MN/AZ/FL; primary completion est. 2027-05) - cutaneous/PCFCL eligibility UNCONFIRMED ('follicle center' wording the hinge): per-protocol check required - WEB-VERIFIED 2026-08-19

JAMA 2016;316(20):2094-2103 (PMID 27893130, NCT02207322) — abstract read firsthand 2026-09-10. POPULATION CAUTION, added at that read because the previous label named no population at all: this is a SINGLE-INSTITUTION randomized trial of 160 adults with HAEMATOLOGICAL malignancy hospitalized for autologous or allogeneic stem-cell transplantation, and its outcomes are quality of life, depression, anxiety, fatigue and symptom burden — it reports no survival and no adverse-event table. It is the factory's standing anchor for the PRINCIPLE that palliative care runs alongside active treatment rather than after it; it is not evidence in this tumour type and is not the source of any number on this card.

refs.label: HBV SCREENING (the reactivation law): Hwang et al., 'Hepatitis B Virus Screening and Management for Patients With Cancer Prior to Therapy: ASCO Provisional Clinical Opinion Update' (J Clin Oncol 2020;38:3698-3715 - PMID 32716741, pubmed-eutils abstract read 2026-08-27): ALL patients anticipating systemic anticancer therapy tested with 3 tests (HBsAg, anti-HBc total Ig/IgG, anti-HBs) WITHOUT delaying therapy. Chronic HBV (HBsAg+): antiviral prophylaxis through and >=12 months after therapy. Past HBV (HBsAg-/anti-HBc+) + HIGH-RISK therapy (anti-CD20 antibodies, SCT): prophylaxis during and >=12 months after; monitoring only as an adherence-dependent alternative.

CARDIAC DYSFUNCTION PREVENTION/MONITORING: Armenian et al., ASCO Clinical Practice Guideline (J Clin Oncol 2017;35:893-911 - PMID 27918725, pubmed-eutils abstract read 2026-08-27): initiate the cardiac-dysfunction discussion BEFORE beginning therapy where risk is sufficiently high; higher-risk populations may benefit from prevention and screening strategies during cancer-directed therapy; keep clinical suspicion high and the evaluation threshold low after potentially cardiotoxic therapy. Companion European framework: 2022 ESC cardio-oncology guidelines (PMID 36017568, esummary-verified).
